title: The Square-Root Rule
hook: A handful of people on your team are carrying way more than you think.
statement: Roughly the square root of your headcount produces about half of all the output.
explainer: Output is never spread evenly. A small core does a huge share. Know who they are, because losing one of them hurts way more than losing an average contributor.
sop: Count Total People on one team or function.
Take the square root to estimate your Top Producers.
Name who they are by output, not title or tenure.
Build retention and growth plans around them.
Recheck as you grow. If headcount jumps but the core doesn't, output per person is slipping.
equation_example: 100 people on a team. √100 = 10 people doing about half the work. And that core grows slowly. 400 people still means only about 20. The bigger you get, the more those few matter.
question: Write down the names of the few people whose loss would hurt your output most.
closing_statement: Protect the few who carry the weight.
caption:
Principle Nº 333: The Square-Root Rule

A handful of people on your team are carrying way more than you think.

Roughly the square root of your headcount produces about half of all the output.

Your turn: Write down the names of the few people whose loss would hurt your output most.
